text: If your friend has $10,000 they won’t need for a few years, I’d recommend considering a high-yield savings account or a CD (certificate of deposit) for that money. It’s safe and will earn some interest without the risk of losing principal. If they’re open to it, investing in a low-cost index fund is another option to consider, especially since they have a longer time horizon. Just remind them to reassess their comfort with risk and keep some liquidity in case they need access to cash. Always good to have an emergency fund as well!

If your friend has $10,000 they won’t need for a few years, I’d suggest putting that money into a high-yield savings account or a short-term certificate of deposit (CD). This way, they can earn some interest without taking on much risk, which is always a good approach in my book. If they’re open to a slightly longer investment horizon, a conservative index fund could also be an option—just remind them it’s important to be ready for some market ups and downs. But really, keeping it accessible while it grows is key, especially since they might need it in the near future. Also, with a rescue dog now, maybe they want to think about some funds for unexpected pup expenses!
